version.changelog:
- Improved API key setup instructions with updated security best practices, including recommendations for limited-scope keys and never storing API keys in source control.
- Clarified that the master skill itself does not access or use the API key—downstream skills require it.
- Provided specific guidance on environment variable management and `.gitignore` usage.
- No functional or behavioral changes to the skill; documentation update only.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: glm-master-skill
Version: 1.0.7

The glm-master-skill is a documentation-only bundle that serves as a directory for the GLM ecosystem (OCR, Image, and Vision skills). It contains no executable code, scripts, or risky instructions, and explicitly avoids using subprocesses to minimize security risks. It provides standard installation commands using npx clawhub and links to official GitHub repositories under the zai-org organization.

llm.summary: This is a documentation-only skill that only catalogs GLM-related skills and installation methods; its contents, requirements, and instructions are coherent with that purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim a documentation-only master skill; the skill is instruction-only, requests no env vars/binaries, and points to official repos and install commands — all consistent with a guide.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md stays within guide scope (catalog, recommended install commands, and advice). It mentions the downstream ZHIPU_API_KEY (as required by many downstream skills) but does not read or require it itself. It instructs agents to open other skills' SKILL.md for specifics. One operational note: it recommends using `npx clawhub@latest`, which will execute code fetched from npm when run — normal for installers but worth vetting before execution.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec for this skill itself (lowest risk). The document recommends `npx clawhub@latest` and Git cloning for downstream skills; `git clone` is fine, while `npx` will fetch and run code from npm, which is common but carries the usual trust/risk tradeoffs (inspect the package or prefer pinned versions).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The master skill does not require any credentials or config paths. It only advises that many downstream GLM skills use ZHIPU_API_KEY and gives security best-practices for handling that key — advisory behavior is proportional.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no install or code means no persistent or privileged presence is requested. The skill does not attempt to change agent/system configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is a read-only catalog and appears safe to install/use. Before running any recommended install commands: 1) vet the `clawhub` npm package (npx will execute code fetched from the registry) or prefer cloning the specific GitHub repo and inspecting its SKILL.md and install steps; 2) only provide ZHIPU_API_KEY (or any API key) to downstream skills you trust — create limited-scope keys, store them in environment variables, and never commit them; 3) review any install scripts or packages referenced by downstream skills before executing them; and 4) consider pinning versions rather than using `@latest` for reproducibility and safety.
